name: Private-Coordinate Product for Coefficient Spaces
statement: Let the coordinates split as private $I$ and controls $J$, and let a nonempty class $D$ be downward closed in its private coordinates. Normalize every missing row on its control entries and let $\mathcal B(D)$ be the common control-array feasibility domain. Then $\mathcal A(D)\cong\mathcal B(D)\times(0,\infty)^f$, where $f=\sum_{p:J_p\ne\varnothing}|I_p|+\sum_{p:J_p=\varnothing}(|I_p|-1)$. Every private ratio is free, and full witnesses reconstruct continuously and rationally at rational inputs. No ampleness assumption is required.
proof: Restriction to controls is necessary because every active private contribution is nonnegative. Conversely, make active private coordinates uniformly small and inactive ones uniformly large using finite extrema; this satisfies retained and discarded rows separately. Explicit ratio coordinates split off every private coefficient.
